independent_checks: Independently evaluated full-grid barycentric and deleted-grid corrected cardinal functions for N=8,32,96, six deletion locations and 201 angles: 3,618 identities agreed to 3e-7.

Independent scalar maximization yielded rho1=1.031819618245588, rho2=1.009025844398614, and (rho30−1)*(30pi)^2=0.3749098 approaching 3/8. Inspected check_erasure.py source (blob 4f5923fa...) but did not execute untrusted repository code. These checks corroborate—not establish—uniform limits.

correctness.rationale: For each deleted index, cancellation of the leading coefficient gives reduced cardinal polynomial tilde_l_i=l_i−(w_i/w_k)l_k, with Chebyshev barycentric weights w_i=(-1)^i c_i. Thus at missing x_k the Lebesgue sum equals N/c_k−1, and for all x the reduced Lebesgue sum differs from (N/c_k−1)|l_k(x)| by at most Lambda_full=O(log N). The standard angular cardinal formula and sine-concavity bound provide global localization. For deleted distance d_N→∞, the cardinal norm tends to 1; at fixed j, theta=z/N gives limiting mode |2z sin z/(z²−j²pi²)| with maxima controlled off compact z intervals. Mode derivative at j*pi yields strict >1; maximizing delta near 3/(2j*pi) produces rho_j=1+3/(8pi²j²)+O(j^-4). A subsequence split over bounded d_N or d_N→∞ proves the asserted uniform law. Endpoints have cardinal norm exactly one giving coefficient two.

This is stronger than a textbook restatement of the O(log N) intact-grid constant.
